openrouter-reasoning-signatures.purpose: OPENROUTER's reasoning-signature transform: addOpenRouterSignatures (prompt-converters.js:1397-1451) rewrites a prior assistant message's `signature` into a `reasoning_details` entry of `type: reasoning.encrypted`, ids the entry `signature-<n>` when the signature is message-level, DELETES the `signature` member, and stamps a per-model `format`. This scenario uses an Anthropic model so the format is `anthropic-claude-v1` (prompt-converters.js:1402-1404), and it also carries a signature on a TOOL CALL, which is added with the tool call's own id instead of a generated one (prompt-converters.js:1439-1446) -- two different id rules in one recorded body. The message-level half is gated on `gemini.thoughtSignatures`, which defaults to TRUE (prompt-converters.js:34, default/config.yaml:382); with the default the entry is produced, and the separate absent-flag scenario records the other branch.
openrouter-reasoning-signatures.stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.
openrouter-reasoning-signatures.comparisonRule: Assert on bodySha256 and bodyLength, which cover the exact bytes. bodyText is a readability projection only and must never be compared: a byte-level encoding difference would round-trip away.
